title: Search (inverted index, Elasticsearch, ranking, autocomplete indexing)
relevance: High — keyword/product/tweet search and typeahead appear constantly in HLD rounds; FAANG + Indian product cos (Flipkart, Uber, Atlassian) expect inverted index + ranking, and often a separate autocomplete design.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad staples are Twitter/YouTube/e-commerce search and autocomplete/typeahead (inverted index + basic ranking + cache). Mid-level expects ES/Lucene internals (segments, shards, BM25), async indexing consistency, and autocomplete precompute vs freshness. Frequency is high whenever the product has a search box; autocomplete is often a standalone Google/Amazon/Meta-style question.

phases.goal: Establish what an inverted index is, how analysis feeds it, and why it beats scanning or SQL LIKE for retrieval.

must_hit.point: An inverted index maps term → postings list (doc IDs, often tf + positions); a query looks up terms, intersects/unions postings, then ranks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate draws term→postings and says retrieval is intersect/union of postings followed by ranking, not scanning documents.

must_hit.point: A forward index (doc → terms) is for display/snippets, not for retrieval.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate clearly separates forward index (show/snippet) from inverted index (find matching docs).

must_hit.point: Analysis (lowercase, stop words, stemming/lemmatization, synonyms) must use agreeing index-time and query-time analyzers or you get silent misses; positions enable phrase/proximity queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names analyzer agreement and says positions are what make phrase/proximity queries possible.

must_hit.point: SQL LIKE '%foo%' forces full-scan / leading-wildcard pain; an inverted index avoids that, while Postgres tsvector/GIN can be good enough for smaller needs vs a dedicated search system.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts leading-wildcard full scan with inverted lookup and names when Postgres FTS is enough.

probes: For docs {1: "red fox", 2: "fox jumps", 3: "red car"}, draw the inverted index, execute red AND fox by intersection, and say what positions add for the phrase "red fox".
Why is SQL LIKE '%foo%' a bad search plan compared to an inverted index?

hints.1: Start from term → list of doc IDs, then think how AND would combine two lists.
hints.2: Build postings for red and fox, intersect them, then mention storing positions beside doc IDs for phrase checks.
hints.3: red → [1,3], fox → [1,2], intersection = [1]; positions let you require adjacent tokens for "red fox" instead of just both terms present.

phases.goal: Explain Lucene/ES segment and shard mechanics, near-real-time indexing, BM25 ranking, and how autocomplete indexing differs from full-text search.

must_hit.point: Lucene buffers then flushes immutable segments and merges them in the background; deletes are soft until merge (LSM-like write amp vs read amp).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes buffer → immutable segment flush → background merge and soft deletes until merge.

must_hit.point: Elasticsearch layout is cluster → index → primary shards (+ replicas); each shard is a Lucene index; queries scatter-gather and p99 tracks the slowest shard; prefer document-partitioned shards over term-sharding for multi-term queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names shard=Lucene index, scatter-gather, slowest-shard p99, and document partitioning preference.

must_hit.point: Refresh makes new segments searchable (default ~1s); under bulk reindex/high write load raise refresh_interval; source of truth is usually OLTP DB with async index via queue/CDC — ES is a derived search store.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate mentions ~1s refresh, tuning refresh_interval, and async/CDC derived-index path rather than ES as system of record.

must_hit.point: BM25 default relevance combines term rarity (IDF), saturated TF (k1), and doc-length normalization (b); interviews often add freshness/popularity/CTR/personalization/business boosts in a multi-stage cascade.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate explains IDF + saturated TF + length norm and may mention cheaper retrieval then heavier re-rank.

must_hit.point: Autocomplete is not full-text search: latency budget is often <100ms; canonical pattern is a prefix structure (trie/FST) with precomputed top-K per prefix so the online path is a lookup, not subtree scan + sort.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate cites <100ms and precomputed top-K on a trie/FST as a lookup, not DFS+sort at query time.

must_hit.point: ES autocomplete options: completion suggester (fast in-memory FST, prefix-oriented) vs search_as_you_type / edge n-grams (more flexible matching, larger index).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts completion suggester FST speed with edge n-gram / search_as_you_type flexibility and index size.

probes: Walk the index pipeline after a user creates a product/tweet: where does freshness lag come from?
Two docs both contain "elastic"; one is 20 tokens, one is 2000. Which ranks higher for query elastic and why, and what does raising k1 change?
Prefix "app": why store top-K completions on the trie node instead of DFS+sort at query time?

hints.1: Separate the primary write from when the search replica becomes visible, and think about TF saturation and document length.
hints.2: DB commit → queue → indexer → ES; BM25 length norm (b) prefers the shorter doc; autocomplete should precompute top-K at the prefix node.
hints.3: Default refresh ~1s (raise refresh_interval under heavy writes); shorter 20-token doc ranks higher via b; raising k1 lessens TF saturation; online typeahead is a top-K lookup on trie/FST, not a scan.

phases.goal: Force clear choices among ES vs lighter search, autocomplete structures, update amplification, and freshness vs precompute.

must_hit.point: Do not use ES as the transactional system of record: avoid it when you need strong transactional truth, heavy point updates of single fields, or a tiny corpus where Postgres FTS / a simple Redis inverted map is enough.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says ES is a search/analytics secondary index and names when Postgres FTS or Redis postings suffice.

must_hit.point: Autocomplete update path should log queries → aggregate frequencies → rebuild suggestion index → atomic swap; trending uses a short-window overlay (e.g. Redis) merged at serve time — do not mutate the hot trie on every search.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes batch/stream rebuild with atomic swap plus a short-window trending overlay rather than per-query trie mutation.

must_hit.point: Custom trie/FST + cache fits ultra-low latency and simple popularity ranking; ES completion / search-as-you-type fits ops simplicity when fuzzy/infix matter more.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate picks trie/top-K for custom typeahead latency and ES suggester when already on ES / needing fuzzy-infix.

must_hit.point: Lucene field updates are approximately delete + reindex of the whole document, causing write amplification — denormalize carefully.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate states whole-doc reindex on update and links that to careful denormalization.

probes: When would you not introduce Elasticsearch and what would you use instead?
Trie vs Elasticsearch for typeahead — how do you choose?
How do trending/breaking-news suggestions appear before the next full autocomplete rebuild?

hints.1: Ask whether you need a transactional primary and how hard single-field updates or tiny corpora make ES.
hints.2: Contrast derived search store + async indexing with OLTP/Postgres FTS/Redis; contrast precomputed trie top-K with ES completion/search-as-you-type.
hints.3: Skip ES for SoT/point-update/tiny corpus; custom trie/FST for <100ms popularity typeahead; ES suggester for ops/fuzzy-infix; serve trends from a short-window Redis overlay merged at read time after atomic swap of the rebuilt index.

phases.goal: Apply inverted index, async ES indexing, shard fan-out, and autocomplete precompute patterns in concrete HLD designs.

must_hit.point: For product/tweet search, sketch write path primary DB commit → queue → indexer → ES, and call out freshness lag, dual-write failure modes, and how you would reindex.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate draws async derived indexing and names lag, dual-write risk, and rebuild/reindex strategy.

must_hit.point: For typeahead, storing top-5 completions on the trie node beats DFS+sort at query time; rebuild on an aggregate schedule and surface breaking news via a short-window overlay before the next full rebuild.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate justifies on-node top-5, scheduled rebuild, and overlay for trends before rebuild.

must_hit.point: With 64 shards a query that must touch all is dominated by the slowest shard; mitigations include replicas, hedged requests, time-based indices, or routing by user.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says tail latency follows the slowest of 64 shards and names at least one mitigation from that list.

must_hit.point: Interview add-on ranking beyond BM25 uses freshness, popularity/CTR, personalization, or business boosts, often as a multi-stage cascade (cheap retrieval → heavier re-rank).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate layers business/freshness/popularity signals after BM25-style retrieval rather than one giant score.

probes: Design Twitter or e-commerce keyword search end-to-end, including indexing and ranking.
Design autocomplete for a Google/Amazon-style typeahead with a brutal latency budget.
If you have 64 shards and every query fans out, what dominates latency and how do you mitigate it?

hints.1: Keep search as a separate derived index path from the primary timeline/catalog store.
hints.2: Tokenize → inverted index / ES cluster → scatter-gather → merge/rank; for typeahead use trie/FST + precomputed top-K and async rebuild.
hints.3: DB → queue/CDC → indexer → ES (~1s refresh lag); rank with BM25 then freshness/popularity; typeahead top-5 on prefix nodes with Redis trending overlay; 64-shard fan-out limited by slowest shard, mitigated by replicas, hedged requests, time-based indices, or user routing.

tradeoffs.topic: Elasticsearch vs Postgres FTS / Redis inverted map
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use ES/Lucene when you need distributed full-text search, ranking, and scale; skip it for strong transactional source of truth, heavy single-field point updates, or tiny corpora where Postgres tsvector/GIN or a simple Redis inverted map is enough.
Prefer document-partitioned shards so multi-term queries fan out cleanly over Lucene shards; term-sharding is a poor default for multi-term interview designs.
Default refresh (~1s) makes new segments searchable quickly; under bulk reindex or high write load raise refresh_interval and accept more lag because ES is a derived store fed asynchronously.

tradeoffs.topic: Custom trie/FST top-K vs Elasticsearch completion / search-as-you-type
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Custom trie/FST with precomputed top-K and cache wins for ultra-low latency and simple popularity ranking; ES completion suggester or search_as_you_type/edge n-grams wins when you already run ES and want ops simplicity or fuzzy/infix matching at the cost of a larger or less prefix-specialized index.

tradeoffs.topic: Precomputed autocomplete rebuild vs trending freshness
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Rebuild suggestions offline/stream-aggregate then atomically swap; serve trending via a short-window overlay (e.g. Redis) merged at read time instead of mutating the hot trie on every search.
Keep BM25 (IDF + saturated TF via k1 + length norm via b) as the cheap default retriever, then cascade freshness, popularity/CTR, personalization, and business boosts in heavier re-rank stages.

gotchas.trap: Treating Elasticsearch as the primary database for money/orders or other transactional truth.
gotchas.correction: ES is a search/analytics secondary index: plan rebuild, lag, and inconsistency with the OLTP primary.

gotchas.trap: Assuming updating one field in a big document is cheap.
gotchas.correction: Lucene updates are approximately delete + reindex of the whole document, so expect write amplification and denormalize carefully.
It is expensive; prefer search_after / cursor-style pagination.

gotchas.trap: Hand-waving phrases and typo tolerance as free features.
gotchas.correction: Positions enable phrases; fuzziness, n-grams, and suggesters handle typos but are costly — gate by prefix length.

gotchas.trap: Using full-text search mechanics for typeahead or mutating a hot trie on every query.
gotchas.correction: Autocomplete needs prefix structures with precomputed top-K and atomic rebuild/swap; use a short-window overlay for trends; choose custom trie/FST for ultra-low latency or ES completion when ops/fuzzy-infix matter more.

gotchas.trap: Ranking heavily on hot terms / stop words with huge postings.
gotchas.correction: Remove stop words, use champion lists, or avoid ranking on ultra-common terms alone.
